name: postfx
description: Effects on the whole picture of the world, as a camera would add them: a soft glow around bright things, darkened corners, film grain, a colour grade, and black bars for a cinematic moment. The interface is drawn after them and never touched. Presentation only: nothing in the simulation changes.

components.name: Effects
components.description: The effects of the picture (only the oldest Effects is used; put it on the camera, for example). bloom (0 to 1) makes bright parts glow over what is around them. vignette (0 to 1) darkens the corners, from vignette_size (the share of the way from the middle to a corner where it starts; below 0 it reaches the middle too, and at -4 it covers almost the whole picture), in vignette_red, vignette_green and vignette_blue (0 to 255; black by default). edge_glow (0 to 1), edge_glow_size and edge_glow_red, edge_glow_green and edge_glow_blue do the same with a second colour laid over it (white by default: the edges of the picture whiten, as when the light becomes too much). grain (0 to 1) lays a fine moving grain, as on film. tint_red, tint_green and tint_blue (0 to 255) multiply every colour (255, 255, 255 changes nothing: a cold night is blue, a warm evening orange); lift_red, lift_green and lift_blue are added everywhere (0 changes nothing: dark parts take that colour). letterbox (0 to 1) is the share of the height covered by black bars at the top and bottom; a tween can slide it in and out for a cut scene. rays (0 to 1) draws shafts of light out of the bright parts, away from the point rays_x, rays_y of the screen (shares of its width and height, 0.5 and 0.5 its middle), rays_length (a share of the screen, 0 to 1) long: light through mist, a sun behind trees. blur (0 to 1) softens the whole picture, from sharp to a few soft blots; paused_blur is used instead while the game is paused (app Time paused), so that the world behind a pause menu cannot be studied.

systems.name: apply
systems.description: Tells the renderer the effects of the frame, from the oldest Effects.
